title: Design LRU-K Cache
description:
Design an **LRU-K** cache `LRUKCache` that evicts entries using their backward `k`-th access time (used in database buffer pools to resist one-time sequential scans):
- `LRUKCache(int capacity, int k)` initializes an empty cache with positive `capacity` and history window `k >= 1`.
- Maintain a monotonically increasing logical clock `tick` (starting at `0`) that increments by `1` on every `put` call and every successful `get` hit (cache misses on `get` do not advance `tick`). Each cached key stores a FIFO queue of up to its `k` most recent access ticks while in the cache.
- `int get(int key)`: if `key` is absent, return `-1`; otherwise record a new access tick for `key` and return its value.
- `void put(int key, int value)`: if `key` already exists, update its value and record a new access tick. If `key` is new and the cache is at `capacity`, evict one entry according to the **LRU-K rule**:
  1. Any entry with **fewer than `k`** accesses is evicted before any entry with `k` accesses; among entries with `< k` accesses, evict the one with the **earliest first access**.
  2. If all cached entries have `k` accesses, evict the entry whose **`k`-th most recent access** (the oldest tick in its length-`k` history) is the **smallest**.
  Then insert `(key, value)` with a fresh single-element access history `[tick]`.

Aim for `O(log capacity)` amortized time per operation.
constraints: At most 2000 calls will be made to get and put.
hints: For every cached key, maintain a bounded deque `hist` of length at most `k`: `tier = 0 if len(hist) < k else 1`, and `hist[0]` is ALWAYS the exact comparison key (earliest access when `tier == 0`, or `k`-th most recent access when `tier == 1`).
Use a lazy-deletion min-heap storing `(tier, hist[0], version, key)` with a globally monotonic `version` counter so re-inserted keys never collide with stale heap entries.

examples.explanation: With cap=2, k=2: key 1 reaches 2 accesses via get(1) while key 2 has only 1, so put(3,30) evicts key 2; after get(3), key 1's 2nd-recent tick (1) < key 3's (4), so put(4,40) evicts key 1.
With k=1, LRU-1 behaves identically to a standard LRU cache: get(1) refreshes 1, so put(3,30) evicts key 2.
Updating an existing key via put(1, 15) counts as an access, giving key 1 two accesses so put(3, 30) evicts key 2.
